Elaine — quick tech notes to bring to the orientation so your Platform team can prep. Short and actionable so SREs can implement hooks quickly.

1) Trace headers we recommend you propagate: X-Trace-Id (UUID v4), X-Parent-Id (span id), X-Sampled (0/1)
   - Example: X-Trace-Id: 8f14e45f-ea9c-4d3c-9b5b-7a1f3f4c1a2b
2) Sampling guidance:
   - Default: 1% global sample for production token-level requests to avoid high egress.
   - Elevated: 5-10% for new models and can be 20% for canary windows.
3) Instrumentation points:
   - Inference entry service (before tokenization) — capture model_name, model_version, prompt_length, response_length
   - Routing layer — capture route_id and fallback_reason when fallback occurs
   - Retry/timeout path — surface timeout_ms and retry_count as tags
4) Error taxonomy (draft mapping):
   - RedwoodError::ModelOOM -> Severity=P2 (requires immediate mitigation, usually scale/quantization)
   - RedwoodError::Timeout -> Severity=P1 if >10% of requests at P95 latency
   - RedwoodError::BadInput -> Severity=P4 (client-side validation suggested)

I pasted a tiny instrumentation snippet (Node/Express) below you can share with eng: 

// middleware to attach trace header to requests
function attachTraceHeaders(req, res, next) {
  req.headers['x-trace-id'] = req.headers['x-trace-id'] || uuid.v4();
  req.headers['x-sampled'] = req.headers['x-sampled'] || (Math.random() < 0.01 ? '1' : '0');
  next();
}

We’ll walk through these live in the meeting and align sampling with your expected QPS.

—Ben
